definition: the way in which a child is cared for and taught by its parents
example: A strict upbringing does not necessarily produce more disciplined adults than a relaxed one.

definition: a person's child or children, or the young of an animal
example: Many parents sacrifice their own leisure time to improve the prospects of their offspring.

definition: a brother or sister
example: Children with an older sibling often acquire language skills more quickly than only children.

definition: all the people who live together in one home
example: The average household now spends a larger share of its income on housing than it did a generation ago.

definition: a relationship based on family connection or shared ancestry
example: In many rural societies, kinship networks provide the main source of support in times of hardship.

definition: a person who relies on another, usually a relative, for financial support
example: Workers with several dependants often struggle to save money for their own retirement.

definition: a person legally responsible for the care of a child who is not their own
paraphrases: person with legal charge of a child
example: Applicants under sixteen must obtain written consent from a parent or legal guardian.

definition: a person's line of descent from an ancestor
example: Some cultures place great value on tracing a family's lineage back many centuries.

definition: the family and origins from which a person is descended
example: Online databases have made it far easier for ordinary people to research their ancestry.

definition: money or property received from someone after their death
example: Rising property prices mean that inheritance now matters more to young adults than their own salaries.

definition: a person who has the legal right to receive property or a title after someone dies
example: As the only heir, she took over the management of the family estate at the age of twenty.

definition: the state of having lost a close relative or friend through death
example: Employers who grant paid time off after a bereavement tend to retain more loyal staff.

definition: having lost a husband or wife through death and not remarried
example: Widowed pensioners are often at greater risk of social isolation than married couples.

definition: to live together as partners without being married
paraphrases: share a home as a couple
example: A growing number of couples cohabit for several years before deciding to marry.

definition: the practice of living together as a couple without being married
example: Cohabitation has become widely accepted in many countries over the past fifty years.

definition: the legal ending of a marriage
example: The divorce rate has fallen in several countries as couples tend to marry later.

definition: a period or arrangement in which a couple live apart
example: The separation of parents can affect a child's confidence, though the effects are often short-lived.

definition: the legal right to look after a child, especially after parents separate
example: Courts usually grant joint custody unless there is evidence that one parent is unfit.

definition: relating to marriage or to the relationship between husband and wife
example: Research suggests that financial stress is a leading cause of marital breakdown.

definition: the state of being married, used in formal contexts
example: Traditional ceremonies often emphasise the permanence of the vows taken in matrimony.

definition: a husband or wife
example: Many countries now allow the spouse of a skilled migrant to work without restriction.

definition: to care for and encourage the growth or development of someone
example: Parents who nurture curiosity early in life often raise children who enjoy learning independently.

definition: to encourage the development of something, or to care for a child who is not one's own
example: Shared mealtimes foster a sense of belonging among children and teenagers.

definition: to legally take another person's child into one's own family
example: Couples who cannot conceive often choose to adopt a child from another country.

definition: the legal process of taking another person's child into one's family
example: Adoption can give vulnerable children a stable home, although the process is often slow.

definition: a close emotional connection between people
example: A strong bond between a mother and her newborn is thought to support healthy development.

definition: the activity of raising and caring for children
example: Different parenting styles can lead to quite different outcomes in teenage behaviour.

definition: describing a parenting style that combines clear rules with warmth and support
example: Studies often link authoritative parenting with higher confidence and better social skills.

definition: allowing a great deal of freedom, with few rules or restrictions
example: Critics argue that permissive parents may struggle to teach children self-control.

definition: trying too hard to protect someone from any risk or difficulty
example: Overprotective parents may unintentionally stop their children from developing resilience.

definition: a person who believes in strict obedience and enforces rules firmly
example: His father was a stern disciplinarian who expected silence at the dinner table.

definition: a person whose behaviour is copied by others, especially young people
example: Parents are often the first role model a child encounters in daily life.

definition: the difference in attitudes and values between older and younger people
example: Technology has widened the generation gap, as grandparents struggle with the devices teenagers use daily.

definition: involving or affecting different age groups within a family or society
example: Intergenerational projects that pair teenagers with pensioners can reduce stereotypes on both sides.

definition: a family group that includes grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins as well as parents and children
paraphrases: relatives beyond the parents and children
example: In an extended family, grandparents often share the responsibility of looking after young children.

definition: a family unit consisting only of two parents and their children
example: Urbanisation has encouraged the spread of the nuclear family in places where extended households once dominated.

definition: describing a family headed by only one mother or father
example: Single-parent households are more likely to rely on affordable childcare to stay in employment.

definition: the care of children, especially while their parents are at work
example: The high cost of childcare discourages some mothers from returning to full-time employment.

definition: the member of a family who earns the money to support the others
example: In many households, women have become the main breadwinner as male employment has declined.

definition: a person who manages a home and family rather than working outside it
example: The unpaid labour of the homemaker is rarely reflected in national economic statistics.

definition: describing a parent who looks after the children and house instead of taking paid work
example: The number of stay-at-home fathers has risen as couples share responsibilities more evenly.

definition: describing a household in which both partners earn a salary
example: Dual-income couples can afford larger mortgages, which may push up property prices.

definition: the routine tasks needed to keep a home clean and tidy
example: Women still perform a larger share of household chores in most developed countries.

definition: a person who looks after someone who is young, old or ill
example: Unpaid family caregivers save governments billions each year in social-care costs.

definition: relating to the duties or feelings of a son or daughter towards their parents
example: In some societies, a strong sense of filial duty means adult children expect to support ageing parents.

definition: relating to or typical of a family
example: Familial obligations can limit the career choices of young adults in close-knit communities.

definition: competition or jealousy between brothers and sisters
example: Giving each child individual attention can reduce sibling rivalry in the home.

definition: a young child who is just learning to walk
example: A toddler begins to understand rules only when adults apply them consistently.

definition: the period of life between childhood and adulthood
example: Peer influence tends to peak during adolescence, when teenagers seek approval from friends.

definition: a young person who is developing from a child into an adult
example: Every adolescent needs space to experiment with independence while still receiving guidance.

definition: having an important and lasting influence on a person's development
example: The formative years of childhood shape attitudes towards money, work and relationships.

definition: a state of relying on someone or something else for support
example: High levels of financial dependency among young adults reflect the cost of housing and study.

definition: unity and mutual support among a group of people
example: Natural disasters often strengthen solidarity between neighbours who had previously barely spoken.

definition: the state of a group being united and working together
example: Shared public spaces can promote social cohesion in diverse communities.

definition: the network of relationships and shared values that holds a society together
collocations: the social fabric of a community
example: Constant relocation for work may weaken the social fabric of small towns.

definition: a standard of behaviour considered typical or acceptable in a society
example: Attitudes to arranged marriage vary, but in some regions it remains the norm.

definition: a social custom that forbids discussion or practice of a subject
example: Discussing mental illness was once a taboo, but openness has grown considerably.

definition: a strong feeling of disapproval that most people in a society have about something
example: There remains a stigma attached to single motherhood in some conservative communities.

definition: a fixed, oversimplified idea about a type of person or thing
example: Children's books that show only women cooking reinforce a damaging stereotype.

definition: to behave in the way that most people in a group or society expect
example: Teenagers often feel pressure to conform to the habits of their friends.

definition: the belief that personal freedom and independence matter more than group needs
example: The growth of individualism has led many people to put personal goals ahead of family duty.

definition: the belief that the needs of the group come before those of the individual
example: In societies shaped by collectivism, major decisions are rarely made by one person alone.

definition: treated as unimportant or pushed to the edge of society
example: Marginalised groups often lack access to the networks that bring job opportunities.

definition: easily harmed or in need of special protection
example: Children and the elderly are especially vulnerable when family support breaks down.

definition: lacking the social or economic conditions needed for a fair chance in life
example: Children from disadvantaged backgrounds often enter school already behind their classmates.

definition: a lack of the basic things that are needed for a decent life
example: Persistent deprivation in early life can have lasting effects on achievement.

definition: a noticeable and often unfair difference between groups
example: The disparity between rural and urban household incomes has widened over the past decade.

definition: to offer to do something without being paid for it
example: Retired residents volunteer at the community centre to teach young people practical skills.

definition: the giving of money or time to help others, especially on a large scale
example: Private philanthropy funds many projects that governments lack the resources to support.

definition: relating to the giving of help to people in need
example: Charitable donations tend to rise sharply after widely reported emergencies.

definition: a person one knows slightly but not well
example: Online platforms make it easy to keep in touch with every casual acquaintance one has ever met.

definition: the pleasant feeling of having someone with you who is a friend
example: Pets can provide companionship for people who live alone.

definition: the state of being alone or separated from other people
example: Social isolation among elderly residents has become a serious concern for local councils.

definition: the influence that people of the same age have on one another's behaviour
example: Many teenagers start unhealthy habits because they cannot resist peer pressure.

definition: a ceremony or event marking an important stage in a person's life
example: In many cultures, a large celebration at eighteen is regarded as a rite of passage.

definition: to reach the age at which one is legally an adult
collocations: the year they came of age
example: Those who come of age during an economic crisis often delay marriage and parenthood.

definition: the situation of parents whose children have grown up and left home
paraphrases: parents whose children have moved out
example: Parents facing an empty nest often rediscover hobbies and friendships they once neglected.

definition: the behaviour and duties that a society expects of men and women
example: Shifting gender roles have encouraged more fathers to take parental leave.

definition: the ability of people to move between social or economic classes
paraphrases: chance to climb the social ladder
example: Access to good schooling remains the most powerful driver of social mobility.
